To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CXCR3, but not CCR2 and not CCR5, is required for T cell trafficking to tumor vascular checkpoints.

CXCR3, but not CCR2 or CCR5, is required to stabilize intravascular adhesions of adoptively transferred effector T cells and that these receptors are non-redundantly required to promote extravasation and tumor infiltration of effector T cells.
CXCR3 is required to stabilize T cells in the tumor vasculature, but that other chemokine receptors, such as CCR5 and CCR2, are dispensable.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of T cell trafficking to tumor vascular sites.
the molecular basis of immune cell trafficking to sites of inflammation.
the role of chemokines and their receptors in the regulation of T cell trafficking in cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CXCR3 signaling is a critical step for CD8 T cell migration across the tumor vascular interface and that this is required for effective T cell-based immunotherapies.
CXCR3 signaling is non-redundantly required for CD8+ T cell trafficking across vascular checkpoints in tumor-bearing hosts.
CXCR3 signaling is required for CD8 T cells to traffic across tumor vascular checkpoints, and that this process is critical for therapeutic efficacy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CXCR3 is a critical checkpoint for CD8 T cell trafficking across the tumor vasculature.
CXCR3 is the key player to guide T cell trafficking to the tumor vascular interface and is essential to the efficacy of adoptive cell transfer therapy.
CXCR3 signaling is required for CD8+ T cell trafficking across tumor vascular checkpoints.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CXCR3 signaling at tumor vessels is required for the trafficking of adoptively transferred tumor-specific CD8+ effector T cells.
CXCR3 is a non-reduntant requirement for T cell trafficking across tumor vascular barriers and is required for effective adoptive immunotherapy.
chemokines and chemokine receptors are not interchangeable.
